text:
In 1990, a massive piece of early internet history ran out of a one-bedroom apartment in Greenwich Village.
 There were no server farms. There were no venture capital meetings.
 There were just dozens of copper phone lines snaking under Stacy Horn’s furniture, connecting to a machine that sounded like a jet engine.
 She was 34 years old.
 She was building an early social network out of her living room.
 Before the cables took over her apartment, Horn was a telecommunications analyst at Mobil Oil.
 The work was stable. The salary was guaranteed.
 She had spent time on a California bulletin board system called the WELL. She saw what happened when people connected through screens.
 She wanted that for New York.
 In 1990, there was no World Wide Web for the public. The internet was just text on a black screen.
 To create a space for people to gather, you had to physically host them.
 Horn quit her corporate job. She took out a loan.
 She bought an Altos computer running the Unix operating system.
 She named her early social network ECHO, the East Coast Hang Out.
 The machine sat in her living room. It generated so much heat she had to keep the windows open in December.
 It cost a fortune to run. Every user required a physical phone line running into the building.
 The first months were quiet.
 To get onto ECHO, users had to own a personal computer, buy a modem, and dial her apartment phone number.
 If someone was already dialed into that specific line, the caller got a busy signal.
 Horn sat in the noise of the cooling fans, watching the screen for activity.
 She invited friends. She told people at parties.
 The users trickled in. They were mostly men who already understood the command line interface.
 Her credit card debt climbed toward $50,000.
 The hardware broke frequently. The phone company did not understand why a residential apartment needed a commercial telecom trunk.
 When the system crashed at three in the morning, Horn had to get out of bed and type manual commands to bring the community back to life.
 At the time, the digital landscape was fundamentally hostile to outsiders. Records from early internet history show it was largely the domain of defense contractors, university researchers, and computer scientists. A 1993 industry survey found that women made up less than five percent of users. Entering a bulletin board system often meant navigating a gauntlet of technical jargon and aggressive gatekeeping. The architecture was not built for social interaction.
 Horn refused to accept those demographics.
 She did not just want computer scientists on her servers. She wanted artists, writers, and ordinary people.
 To break the gender imbalance, she offered free accounts to women for a year.
 It worked.
 ECHO user base eventually became nearly half female. It was a statistical anomaly in the 1990s tech era.
 She spent years managing the human friction of digital life, long before the industry had words for it.
 In 1991, the user base was small enough that Horn knew every handle. They talked about local New York politics, the AIDS crisis, and the shifting culture of the city.
 By 1992, the discussions fractured into specific boards.
 By 1993, the network was self-sustaining. The users were organizing their own offline events, creating a culture entirely separate from her direct control.
 She was essentially inventing community moderation in real time.
 When users fought in the forums, there were no automated algorithms to hide the conflict. Horn had to moderate it herself.
 She established rules of conduct. She taught people how to argue without destroying the space.
 When someone was going through a divorce or a depression, the network rallied around them.
 Horn was not a perfect administrator. She could be impatient. She sometimes lost her temper with demanding users and threatened to delete the accounts of people who annoyed her, exhausted by the relentless demands of being a one-woman customer service department.
 She worked 80-hour weeks.
 The phone lines multiplied. Twenty-two lines. Then thirty.
 The physical weight of the network sat heavily in her living space. She could hear the modems handshaking, a high-pitched screech meaning two humans were connecting through her floorboards.
 To anchor the digital space in reality, she forced the users to meet.
 She hosted ECHO parties in New York. People who had only known each other as green text on a black screen stood in crowded bars, realizing they had formed actual relationships.
 By the mid-1990s, ECHO had thousands of active users.
 It became a cultural fixture in New York.
 Horn had proved the concept. People would pay a monthly subscription not for content, but for each other.
 She figured out user profiles, private messages, threaded conversations, and community guidelines.
 She proved that the internet could be a neighborhood.
 Then the world caught up.
 Silicon Valley recognized the value of what she had built.
 They did not build networks in living rooms. They built them in data centers. With millions in venture capital. Backed by institutional wealth. Designed for global scale. Engineered for maximum extraction.
 They did not charge a monthly fee. They offered access for free, harvesting user data to sell to advertisers.
 Horn had built a business model based on mutual respect and shared cost. Silicon Valley built a business model based on extraction.
 The internet shifted from intimate neighborhoods to massive, monetized cities.
 Horn could not compete with free.
 Her name does not appear in standard textbooks about the creation of the social web.
 She did the work. They built the industry.
 She proved strangers could form a community. A decade later, Silicon Valley proved that community could be sold.
 ECHO continued to run for decades. It transitioned to the web, maintained by a core group of loyalists who remembered what the internet used to feel like.
 The tech industry is now a multi-trillion-dollar machine.
 Social networks run on algorithms designed to harvest attention and provoke anger, optimized for engagement metrics and quarterly earnings.
 The founders of those companies are billionaires. They testify before Congress. They dictate global communication.
 Horn still lives in New York.
 The physical modems are gone from her floorboards. The high-pitched screech of a dial-up connection is a relic.
 The concept of logging on just to belong to a neighborhood has been replaced by the endless scroll.
 Stacy Horn: the woman who wired the first social network.
 Source: Stacy Horn.
 Verified via: The WELL Archives, NYU Internet History Records.

Lecture: 
Not Quite Enough
—Institutional Constraint, 
Personal Exit, 
and the Incomplete Archive

For graduate students in 
Law, 
Political Science, 
Psychiatry, 
and Social Anthropology

Consider two residues. 

The first is institutional. 

A traveling psychiatrist, 
working as a 1099 contractor 
at Pelican Bay State Prison in Crescent City, 
requests a full week of leave 
for grandchildren’s birthdays. 

Five requests are denied 
for lack of staff. 

Four days are offered. 

He resigns. 

Dr. Utecht remains. 

The second residue is digital and older: 
a 2013 Facebook thread 
in which friends coordinate 
a Las Vegas trip. 

Hotel details are missing, 
texts go unanswered, 
someone buys Nikes 
“in case you don’t want to be outdressed,” 
and the plans 
dissolve into comments
 that are later half-lost. 

Both residues 
sit against 
the earlier memory 
that returns as 
“Page Not Found.”

These are ordinary frictions. 

Examined through the required lenses, 
they illustrate 
how systems 
maintain themselves 
by making certain 
absences, 
exits, 
and incomplete coordinations 
structurally necessary.

Self-organizing systems.

Correctional mental health 
at a remote Level IV facility 
organizes around chronic understaffing. 

Coverage is improvised 
through contractors, 
visiting clinicians, 
and the residual presence 
of those who cannot 
or do not leave. 

The system 
does not require 
perfect continuity of personnel; 
it requires continuity 
of minimal function. 

When one contractor exits 
because family obligations 
cannot be absorbed, 
the organization 
reconfigures 
around the remaining clinicians. 

Law 
treats the employment relation 
of a 1099 
as external to the institution’s 
duty to staff itself. 

Political science 
observes the same pattern 
in agencies 
that externalize risk 
to contractors 
while retaining operational control. 

Psychiatry 
notes that 
clinical responsibility 
is distributed across 
whoever remains on site. 

Anthropology 
records how institutions 
produce their own kinship of necessity
—colleagues who stay, 
those who leave
—while the surrounding community continues. 

The Vegas thread 
is a smaller 
self-organizing episode: 
information fails to propagate, 
participants improvise, 
and the plan 
either occurs 
or does not; 
the social form of 
“friends coordinating a trip” 
persists regardless.

Plausible deniability.

The denial of leave 
rests on a staffing shortage 
that the institution 
can treat as given 
rather than as a product 
of its own 
hiring, 
retention, 
and contractor policies. 

The contractor’s resignation 
converts an unmet request 
into a voluntary exit, 
preserving the appearance 
that adequate coverage 
was maintained. 

In law, 
the independent-contractor status 
supplies a ready zone 
of non-liability 
for the institution’s scheduling practices. 

In politics, 
similar deniability 
operates 
when agencies 
rely on temporary personnel 
whose departure 
does not register 
as institutional failure. 

In psychiatry, 
the clinical record continues; 
the individual clinician’s absence 
is absorbed. 

In anthropology, 
institutional narratives 
often attribute exits 
to personal choice 
while the structural conditions 
that made the choice necessary 
remain unexamined. 

The Facebook thread 
performs a lighter version: 
“Never mind Sean, got it”
erases the prior uncertainty 
without resolving 
how the information finally arrived. 

Deniability 
keeps both 
the prison schedule 
and the social plan 
formally intact.

Murphy’s Law.

What can fail 
will fail under constraint. 

Staffing levels 
that leave no margin 
for ordinary family events 
produce denied leave. 

Digital coordination 
that depends on unanswered texts 
and missing hotel names 
produces incomplete plans. 

Hard drives and platforms 
lose the records of both. 

Because information erasure 
carries a thermodynamic cost 
and because every archive 
is finite, 
loss is the expected outcome. 

Legal doctrines
 of constructive notice 
and due diligence 
assume actors 
will absorb such failures.

 Political systems 
treat contractor turnover 
as routine. 

Psychiatric practice 
in understaffed settings 
treats interrupted care 
as the background condition. 

Anthropological method 
treats partial records 
as normal. 

The 2013 thread 
that is now partially illegible 
and the 2015 caption 
that returns as “Page Not Found” 
are simply Murphy’s Law 
operating at the scale 
of personal and institutional memory.

Pandora’s box.

Once the decision to resign is made, 
the prior employment relation 
cannot be restored 
on the same terms. 

Once a digital thread 
is posted, 
its later disappearance 
or partial survival 
cannot be fully reversed. 

Correctional systems 
that open the box 
of contractor reliance 
discover that personnel 
can exit 
when family demands 
exceed institutional flexibility; 

the knowledge 
that coverage 
depends on individuals 
who may leave 
is irreversible. 

Digital platforms 
that record ordinary coordination 
make those records 
both persistent and fragile. 

Law 
confronts 
the difficulty 
of reconstructing intent 
after the fact. 

Political analysis 
notes 
hat temporary staffing 
creates permanent dependencies. 

Psychiatry 
observes that clinical relationships 
interrupted by institutional constraint 
leave residual effects 
that cannot be fully closed. 

Anthropology 
records 
how the introduction 
of digital mediation
 changes the durability
of social plans. 

The box, 
once opened, 
yields both 
the possibility 
of exit 
and the incompleteness 
of the remaining record.

The butterfly effect.

A denied week of leave 
for two birthdays 
produces a resignation. 

That resignation 
leaves one clinician in place 
and removes another. 

Small differences
in staffing margin, 
in the timing of family events, 
or in the content 
of a single text message
about a hotel 
produce divergent trajectories. 

In law, 
minor variations
in contractor status 
or notice requirements 
can determine liability. 

In politics, 
a single retention failure 
can cascade 
into measurable gaps in service. 

In psychiatry, 
the presence 
or absence 
of one clinician 
alters the distribution 
of risk 
for an entire caseload. 

In anthropology, 
contingent decisions 
about presence 
and absence 
reshape local social fields. 

Sensitive dependence 
coexists 
with self-organization: 
the system continues, 
reorganized 
around what remains. 

The arrow of time 
ensures the reorganization is irreversible. 

Neither the precise coverage 
that would have existed 
had the leave been granted, 
nor the precise content 
of the lost digital pages, 
can be recovered.

Across the fields, 
the pattern is consistent. 

Systems maintain themselves 
by converting personal 
and informational shortfalls 
into structural features
—self-organized coverage, 
plausible zones of non-responsibility, 
expected failures,
irreversible openings, 
and sensitive dependence 
on small events. 

The contractor’s exit 
and the incomplete digital thread 
are local instances of the same pressure. 

Forgetting,
whether institutional or digital,
 is licensed b
y the requirement 
that the system continue 
under incomplete information. 

The adjacency of free will 
to the origin of constraints remains open; 
what is observable 
is that both individual exit 
and institutional continuity 
sit at the boundary 
where description 
encounters contingency 
that cannot yet be further reduced.

Everything (Is Never Quite Enough)
(in the manner of Wasis Diop)

Moments take so very long
Who has time to fear the request denied?
Trust set on precedent,
Why should it be the one who stays who decides?

Giving the week a little less
Is taking what the grandchildren need.
Everything is never quite enough.
Let the schedule fake the coverage,

Who has time to chase the missing staff?
Digital is where the thread is;
Plans can always be replaced.
Welcome to the contractor’s exit,

Welcome to the page not found.
Everything is never quite enough.
Can’t see the hotel,
What are you thinking?
Fill in the space, please—

Oh, let me hear you.
Sterilized behind these gates,
Locked behind the green of Crescent City.
Even if the leave had come,
What the coverage was was never clear.

No more words to say to the denied request;
No more thoughts appear of the lost 2015.
Life was taking way too long—
Who had breath to waste on five requests?

Tired of the four-day offer,
Bored with everything the system does.
Every day there’s less of the archive.
Me, I’ve been erased.
Everything is never quite enough.

text:
A college quarterback turned down eight million dollars to stay where he already was.

Today his team beat Tennessee.

The offer was eight million over two years, from a school that wanted him to transfer. He was 19 years old.

Here is what his father said about it.

"He was offered all kinds of crazy numbers."

"We didn't come here to make money."

"If it ain't broke, don't fix it."

His name is LaNorris Sellers. His father is Norris Sellers. They are from Florence, South Carolina.

Understand that this was not a kid with nowhere else to go.

He went to South Florence High School all four years and took them to a state championship as a senior, 57 to 30. He was the player of the year in that town and the offensive MVP of the Shrine Bowl.

He committed to Virginia first. Then he changed it to Syracuse. Then in December of 2022 he signed with South Carolina instead, about an hour and a half up the road from his house.

He sat his first year behind Spencer Rattler and played three games.

Then they gave him the job and he was the best freshman in the Southeastern Conference. He threw for 2,534 yards and ran for 674 more. Nine wins. A top 15 ranking. They beat Missouri, Texas A&M and Clemson in the same season.

That is when the phone calls started.

Here is what he says about why he did not pick up.

"I've built relationships here, my family's here, my brother's here."

His younger brother Jayden plays receiver on the same team.

His father says it was never really a debate.

"There were several talks, but it never really crossed his mind."

Now be honest about the two years since. They went 4 and 8 last season after being ranked tenth in the country, which is about as bad as a year can go. He came into today 2 and 3. He has thrown 19 interceptions in his career and his completion percentage has gone down, not up.

Eight million dollars is also a sum of money most people reading this will never see, and there is no version of this where turning it down was obviously correct.

His father said the quiet part out loud about that.

"Who's gonna say no to eight million dollars for two years?"

The answer is almost nobody, and that is exactly the point.

Teenagers get that call and they go, and they are not wrong to go.

This one stayed, in the state he grew up in, at the school an hour from his mother's house, on a team where his little brother catches his passes.

And today, on a bad season, against the eleventh ranked team in America, the Volunteers came to South Carolina and lost.

Easton Messer is five foot nine. He scored five touchdowns for Florida Atlantic today, and he did it three different ways.

Two of them he caught. Two of them he ran in himself. The fifth one he returned a punt for, and it was the longest punt return touchdown in the history of his school.

He finished with 262 all purpose yards and 12 catches.

He had 14 catches in the game the week before that.

Messer was a two star recruit coming out of high school.

Now here is the part almost nobody knows about him.

He was born in Louisville, Kentucky, and his family moved when he was small. His father is an engineer who ran global operations for his company, and the job kept moving them.

Messer grew up in Costa Rica. Then Panama. Then Malaysia.

He speaks fluent Spanish.

Somewhere in the middle of all that he had to pick between soccer and football, and he picked football, which is not the obvious choice for a kid being raised in Central America and southeast Asia.

Messer came back and went to Christian Academy of Louisville. Two stars. His offers were Air Force, Marshall and Eastern Kentucky.

Western Kentucky took him. He played three games as a freshman and caught one pass all year, a 44 yard touchdown, and then redshirted to save the season.

The next year he caught 42. The year after that, 55.

Then the coach who had recruited him to Western Kentucky, Zach Kittley, got the Florida Atlantic job. Messer followed him, and so did the quarterback, Caden Veltkamp.

In his first season at Florida Atlantic Messer led the entire country in catches per game at 8.67.

In his first game there he caught 15 passes and tied a school record. This year his team voted him a captain.

Here is what he says about playing that way.

"Pressure is a privilege."

But a two star kid who grew up on three different continents, who caught one football his entire freshman season, scored five touchdowns in one afternoon and broke a record that had stood at his school since it opened.

What is the furthest from home you ever had to start over.

text:
lol do u even physics bro? Review: “A Parameter-Free Candidate for the Fine-Structure Constant from Entangled Qudits,” A. D. Wissner-Gross, October 23, 2026

Summary of the claim. The paper reports that a single axiom about maximally entangled pairs yields the algebraic number (79 + 48√2 + 42√3 + 3√6)/31104, whose inverse agrees with the CODATA 2022 value of α⁻¹(0) to ten significant figures, and conjectures that this number is the fine-structure constant.

1. The paper contains no physics. The fine-structure constant is the strength with which the photon field couples to electric charge at zero momentum transfer. Every term in that definition requires a field defined on spacetime, a charged particle, and a scattering process from which the zero-transfer limit is taken. The paper supplies none of these, and says so:

No spacetime. “An axiom about entangled pairs, which mentions neither charge nor spacetime” (Discussion). “The structures they presuppose in field theory, a field over spacetime and a scattering amplitude, are not supplied here” (S8).
No time. “The model has no time order” (S7). Nothing evolves.
No particles. The only particle named is the photon, and it appears solely in Conjecture 1. The object conjectured to be the photon’s link carries hypercharge Y = 1/6, which the author identifies as “the quantum numbers of the left-handed quark doublet” (S3). The photon has hypercharge zero.
No Lagrangian, no Hamiltonian, no equation of motion, no interaction. “The model has no charged loop, no vertex factor, no loop momentum, and no expansion in a coupling” (Fig. S2). “The model constructs no propagator” and “no function of the momentum transfer” (S8).

A coupling constant measures the strength of an interaction. With no interaction present, the quantity computed has no definition as a coupling.

2. What is computed. The computation is finite combinatorics on the operator algebra of C³⊗C². Four slots carry the traceless basis operators of a qutrit (8) and a qubit (3). Products of one operator from each of two distinct slots number 64 + 9 + 4·24 = 169; three qubit commutators bring the count to 172. The records are sorted into four classes by their symmetry under two permutations, the classes are assigned the weights 1, √2, √3, √6, and the weights are summed and divided by 24·36·36, the dimension of a tensor product of operator spaces. Theorem 2 states that the trace of an operator defined to carry these weights, divided by this dimension, equals the sum of these weights divided by this dimension. The Lean file verifies that arithmetic.

3. The physics vocabulary is attached by definition. The author is explicit. “Identifying this normalized readout with the on-shell two-point function is the one definitional identification of the paper. It names what Theorem 2 computes and is used in no proof.” Figure S2 is “a correspondence of roles, not of diagrams.” Table S7 is a glossary mapping each QED term to a counting step. The bare coupling α_bare = 1 is the statement that a projection onto a pure state succeeds with probability one (“½ + ½ = 1”). The Ward identity Z₁ = Z₂ is the statement that the scalar i commutes with every operator. Z₃ is the name given to the number after it is computed.

4. The entangled pairs are not physical systems. A qudit is defined as “a finite-dimensional quantum system, of dimension at least two,” with no observable, location, mass, or charge. Entanglement in quantum mechanics is a correlation between measurement outcomes on two systems; the paper has no second location and discards outcome statistics, since every projection “has no failure branch” and “no expectation value is estimated anywhere.” What remains is the vector Σ|i⟩|i⟩/√d as an algebraic device. Its roles in the paper are to supply the amplitudes 1/√d (the origin of √2 and √3, Theorem S7), the transpose identity that doubles the slot count, the U⊗Ū invariance renamed “gauge freedom,” and the Størmer–Woronowicz–Choi separability threshold d₁d₂ ≤ 6 used to select dimensions 2 and 3.

5. The gauge group is the block decomposition of C⁵. S(U(3)×U(2)) as the subgroup of SU(5) preserving C²⊕C³ is the Georgi–Glashow observation, cited here to Baez–Huerta. Any split of five dimensions into 2 + 3 produces it. The dimensions 2 and 3 are selected by a definition of “fix” constructed so that the separability threshold falls out; the author concedes that “under a weaker definition of fix ... the read cap below would be a premise rather than a consequence.”

6. The number was fitted. The paper states that “nothing in it is fit to α” and prints Table S5: fourteen alternative wordings of its own definitions, each with its inverse evaluated (135.894, 146.524, 127.536, 139.030, 134.485, 112.423, 139.713, 138.348, 132.739, 141.621, 97.505, 70.190, 0.758, 180.837), with the note that “two of them land within one percent of the computed value.” That table cannot be produced without computing every variant and comparing each to 137.036; it is the record of a search. Each row is excluded by a sentence (“a read is an act at the end at which it is taken”; “four letters, a four-point quantity”; “per unit of the conserved count”) and never by a calculation. The object itself is selected from 23 configurations (Table S2) by three conditions stated after the fact; the author notes that “minimality does not select the object” and leaves the other configurations “not evaluated.” The Lean file verifies that the chosen clauses yield the chosen number; it cannot verify when the clauses were chosen. The accompanying mutations script, offered as evidence of rigor, establishes that the result holds for exactly one wording out of many.

7. Postselection by fiat. The join of two links succeeds with probability 1/6 under quantum mechanics. The paper multiplies by √6 and declares the complementary outcome “no configuration of the axiom.” The author acknowledges that “whether a postselected law of this kind is consistent with the rest of physics is not settled here.”

8. Prior art. Wyler (1969, 1971) obtained α⁻¹ ≈ 137.036 from volumes of symmetric domains, and the author cites that work as having “foundered on what fixed their normalization.” The present paper has the same unfixed normalization — the choice of N over 172, of √kᵣ over kᵣ, of which end each exchange acts at — with each free choice renamed a definition.

Recommendation. The paper presents an algebraic number from a counting rule on C³⊗C², with no spacetime, no time, no particles, no Lagrangian, no Hamiltonian, and no interaction, and identifies it with a coupling constant by a glossary. The counting rule has at least three independently adjustable clauses and one configuration choice, each resolved by wording, and the author’s own Table S5 records the evaluation of alternatives against the target. The result belongs to the numerological literature on α that the paper cites, and the Lean verification, the CODATA comparison, and the on-shell vocabulary change the presentation without changing that classification. Reject.

Iranian crude shipments fall to zero under reinstated naval blockade

Outbound deliveries of Iranian crude oil ceased entirely during the month of September, according to records compiled by Kpler. The zero-barrel outcome marked the first total pause in these oil dispatches since monitoring efforts initiated in 2013. This total disruption followed the reimposition of an American naval blockade on July 14 after temporary diplomatic arrangements fell apart. Naval forces from the United States had originally established the interdiction perimeter on April 13 to block Iranian fuel commerce. The timeline links the renewed blockade to the end of the tentative deal, while the zero-export reading shows how sharply crude shipments changed after enforcement resumed.

Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian placed direct blame on Washington for the collapse of an interim compromise intended to halt fighting involving Israel and the United States. Negotiators from Tehran had offered a comprehensive framework aimed at settling the confrontation peacefully. Under that proposal, Iranian officials agreed to lift all transit constraints across the Strait of Hormuz and resume talks over nuclear development. In exchange, the leadership in Tehran demanded that the United States dismantle its maritime blockade and remove economic sanctions. The proposal tied freer passage through the strait and a return to nuclear discussions to Washington lifting the blockade and sanctions, but Pezeshkian said the interim arrangement broke down because of the United States.

The wider armed conflict began on February 28 when American and Israeli units commenced a coordinated military offensive under the designation Epic Fury. The opening day of bombardment resulted in the death of Iran's supreme leader during initial attacks on February 28. Following that fatal strike, Mojtaba Khamenei assumed the office of supreme leader to direct the nation's governance. The military campaign quickly expanded beyond individual targets into a protracted confrontation over regional navigation and sovereignty. The same opening strikes therefore marked both the start of the joint campaign and the loss of Iran's supreme leader, after which Mojtaba Khamenei took over the role.

Addressing rally participants in Florida, Donald Trump indicated that the United States could execute another military offensive against Iran. Trump's declaration about conducting an additional Epic Fury mission is understood as a plan to renew large-scale operations comparable to the late-February campaign. However, Trump stated that the United States would avoid staging strikes on Iranian territory ahead of the midterm voting set for November 3. Political schedules are pressing in both allied capitals, as Israel prepares for parliamentary voting on Tuesday while American congressional contests take place on November 3. His remarks pair the possibility of renewed operations with a stated pause until after the US midterms, while Israel's parliamentary election is scheduled for Tuesday.

Naval deployments have reinforced American positions near Iranian maritime corridors. The aircraft carrier USS Theodore Roosevelt sailed from Japan toward the Arabian Sea to link up with two American aircraft carriers already operating in the area. Forces under United States Central Command have also engaged commercial vessels directly within the Gulf of Oman. In one documented encounter, an American fighter aircraft fired on the propulsion assembly of the merchant vessel Ocean Molica. The carrier's deployment adds to two US carriers already in the Arabian Sea, while the reported strike on Ocean Molica shows that commercial shipping has also been drawn into military action in the Gulf of Oman.

Iran's Armed Forces Chief of Staff Ali Abdollahi declared that American troops would face an absolute ban from entering the Gulf at any time. The Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps declared an intent to bombard American garrisons across the Middle East if US warships maintain protective escort missions through the Strait of Hormuz. Concurrently, the naval division of the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps announced that it had damaged four oil tankers in the strait. The same maritime branch reported that three other commercial ships detonated marine mines within the passage. Taken together, the statements and reported incidents put both US military access and commercial passage through the strait at issue, with the IRGC claiming strikes on four tankers and mines hitting three other vessels.

Despite the severe drop in crude dispatches, other forms of Iranian petroleum exports have continued moving along southern sea lanes. Investigators from the organization United Against Nuclear Iran observed at least eight gas carriers handling Iranian liquefied petroleum gas since the middle of July. These tracked tankers transported liquefied petroleum gas out of the Gulf of Oman despite intensified maritime surveillance. The persistent traffic highlights partial operations by specialized energy transporters navigating outside the halted crude tanker network. The contrast is between crude exports, which Kpler recorded at zero in September, and at least eight LPG tankers tracked carrying Iranian cargo since mid-July; the figures concern different petroleum products and periods.

Iranian military leaders have also issued threats against international communication infrastructure passing near their shoreline. Yadollah Javani stated that Iranian units could destroy seven principal data cables laid along the seabed of the Strait of Hormuz if domestic sites suffer damage. Industry assessments from TeleGeography determine that less than one percent of global digital network throughput crosses the Strait of Hormuz seabed. Regional data facilities have experienced previous attacks, including March strikes in which Iranian forces hit two Amazon Web Services installations inside the United Arab Emirates. The cable threat concerns seven routes, but TeleGeography's estimate indicates that less than one percent of international bandwidth uses the strait; the March strikes on two UAE cloud sites show separate infrastructure has also been hit.

Concerns over direct confrontation extend to covert planning against foreign leaders. Director of National Intelligence Jay Clayton delivered a formal memorandum alerting Marco Rubio to sophisticated Iranian plotting aimed at American government personnel. At the same time, regional allies face ongoing violence from aligned factions outside Iranian territory. Bombardment carried out by Houthi combatants against the international airport serving Riyadh killed 14 individuals during a single weekend. The reported threats and violence affect different groups: Clayton's memo warned of schemes targeting American officials, while the Riyadh airport strikes killed 14 people over one weekend.

With UVA women’s basketball practice underway and a clearer picture of the roster, I believe this group will be on the bubble tu make the NCAA Tournament.

The season depends on Kymora Johnson’s help and whether the frontcourt delivers.

Kymora is the star. She can score, shoot, pass, create, rebound, and control a game. She is one of the best leaders of all time. That goes for Brogdon and other male stars.

But Kymora must trust the offense when defenses force the ball out of her hands. Roussell must create opportunities without asking her tu manufacture every good shot.

Mary-Anna Asare could be the most important addition. Her scoring, ball handling, and experience should relieve Kymora. She could become a difference-maker, but ACC length and pressure will test her finishing and decision-making.

Punish teams that load up on Johnson. In my truth, Kymora hasn’t had a backcourt partner this talented.

Breona Hurd is a swing player. She offers scoring, rebounding, and shooting to stretch defenses. Injuries interrupted her progress, but UVA needs consistency.

Hurd must attack closeouts, pursue rebounds, and shoot confidently. Make opponents respect that talent every night.

Olivia McGhee brings wing size and scoring. As she returns from her ankle injury, rhythm and durability matter, but so does aggression.

Stop waiting for the ball. Cut, attack, and rebound. She can become an important rotation player if her activity matches her ability.

Tabitha Amanze is critical tu this team’s balance. Her interior scoring, offensive rebounding, and shot contests provide something jumpers can’t replace.

Her recovery remains a major variable. When available, feed her inside. She must deliver strong finishes and disciplined defense. A healthy Amanze changes this team.

Caterina Piatti brings size and Florida experience. But my expectations are measured. At 6'4", she can help inside.

How much she helps will depend on finishing through contact, defending reliably, and rebounding against physical opponents.

Adeang Ring has upside, but it’s time for production. At 6'5", she needs tu establish position, pursue rebounds, and make quick decisions. UVA needs somebody dependable for an entire shift.

Janaé Walker projects as a supporting frontcourt player. Her production doesn’t suggest a featured scorer. Rebounding, screening, positioning, and finishing available chances must earn her minutes.

Eris Lester has potential, but coming off a medical redshirt, she must establish her role. UVA needs wing activity, disciplined defense, and somebody who attacks space.

Offensive consistency is the question. Coming from Alabama doesn’t make her an impact player.

Emilie Brzoňová interests me among the freshmen. Her international scoring gives her a foundation tu contribute alongside guards drawing help. Handling pressure, making quick reads, and defending ACC players will determine her minutes.

Sintija Aukštikalnytė brings international scoring and guard rebounding. She deserves an opportunity. Adjusting tu greater length and speed while learning when tu attack or move the ball will be the test.

Erica Gribble arrives with a scorer’s résumé. She must find efficient offense without forcing high school opportunities. Defense and decision-making matter when shots are limited.

She can develop behind experienced guards and earn some time. 

This is my girl, Lyla Coogen. She’s a development player. Her size gives the staff a foundation, but strength, finishing, positioning, and assignments come first.

She must demonstrate ACC readiness. Make early minutes productive and build trust.

Roussell has pieces for movement, spacing, and multiple players attacking openings.

Freedom requires accountability. Careless turnovers, missed rotations, and watching Kymora can’t become habits.

My biggest concern is the frontcourt, especially Amanze’s recovery.

Next is who produces when Kymora gives up the ball. Those answers determine if UVA escapes the bubble in March.

text:
Visited the Applied Digital data center going up outside Center, ND recently. The scale is mind blowing. It sits on a full section, a square mile of former farmland, with an earth wall built around it so you can't really see it driving by. Behind the wall sit cranes and massive concrete shells.

What's going up right now is "only" 300MW of compute in two buildings for an undisclosed hyperscaler 15 year $7.5B base contract. The main building alone is ~907k sq ft, about 20 acres of roof or 15 football fields. This phase is on the order of 120,000 GPUs. At full load it pulls ~430MW from the grid. That's almost 2x what all of Bismarck-Mandan draws, and roughly two-thirds of the electricity used by every home in North Dakota combined.

Next door is the Milton R. Young coal plant. A dragline with a boom longer than a football field scrapes the earth 24/7, and 240-ton trucks haul lignite to the plant. All of that work, burning ~4M tons a year of 60-million-year-old Paleocene swamp, makes 705MW. This one campus would use ~60% of that entire plant's output. Put another way, that's roughly 6,700 tons of coal a day, about 28 of those 240-ton truckloads every day, just to keep the GPUs running.

Then there are the windmills spinning all around it. Each one is 1.5-3MW, but on average the wind only delivers ~40% of nameplate. Powering this site around the clock with wind would take ~350 turbines spread over ~140 square miles, plus storage for calm days.

300MW is just the start. The power will come from a new 1.2GW gas plant right next door (four 300MW units, targeted for 2030), built by Base Electron, which is run by Applied Digital's own CEO and president. On the last earnings call, the CEO said Center is set up for "almost unlimited capacity for expansion." 

For a sense of what that 1.2GW gas plant means: it's 1.7x the coal plant next door, the equivalent of ~1,000 wind turbines on ~400 square miles, ~2x the load of Fargo-Moorhead, and more power than every home in North Dakota uses. All of it next to a town of 583 people.

The other constraint is people. I talked to an electrician on site making ~$140/hr. He's thinking about moving to Texas, where he's been offered ~$400k/yr working on data centers (with overtime and per diem). It takes 8,000 hours and 4-5 years to make a journeyman, so those licenses are in short supply.

It's one thing to run the IRR math on 1GW and say yes, the returns are strong and this is money good. SemiAnalysis is tracking ~50GW of new data center capacity outside China in 2027. It's another thing to stand there and see what 300MW takes, and ask whether we really have the space, power, energy and workers to do this 150+ times over.

These are the largest facilities I've ever seen. Our world will physically look very different ten years from now.

October 24th – A day worth remembering for one of the most significant transactions in American history - 🇺🇸🇺🇸🇺🇸🇺🇸🇺🇸🇺🇸🇺🇸🇺🇸.                                              
Today, October 24th, offers an opportunity to look back at a moment that definitively altered the destiny of the United States: the acquisition of the Louisiana Territory from Napoleon Bonaparte’s France in 1803—a purchase that reshaped the map of America.

In 1803, President Thomas Jefferson sought to secure United States access to the Mississippi River and the strategic port of New Orleans, both of which were vital to American commerce. However, American negotiators received an unexpected offer from France: Napoleon was willing to sell not just New Orleans, but the entire Louisiana Territory.

The agreed-upon price was $15 million for approximately 828,000 square miles of territory—equivalent to over 2.1 million square kilometers. At the nominal value of the time, this amounted to roughly four cents per acre.

Through this transaction, the United States doubled its land area and paved the way for major westward expansion. The acquired territory encompassed lands that today form parts of numerous American states, including Louisiana, Missouri, Iowa, Arkansas, Kansas, and Nebraska.

text:
The Web Was Shared with the World in a Form Others Could Change

A small question
What does it take for something new to spread around the world?

On the screen, numbers like [1] and [2] appear here and there within the text. When you type a number on the keyboard and press Enter, another document appears, the one that number leads to.

This is how people used a program called the line-mode browser in the early days of the Web. It was a tool for reading documents on the Web, and instructions from 1992 describe this way of using it. Rather than clicking on text on the screen, as we often do today, people entered numbers to move from one document to another.

The next document might not be stored on the computer in front of you. When you request a document kept on another computer, a program called a "server" runs there and sends it back. The browser and server also use shared software components for communication and processing documents. What looks like the simple act of entering a single number depends on programs performing different tasks.

But could someone who received this tool also change how it worked? Being allowed to use a finished program is not the same as being allowed to inspect its inner workings, alter them, and pass the program on to someone else.

On April 30, 1993, CERN, a European research institution based in Switzerland, issued a declaration about its Web software. It covered three components: a program for reading documents, server software for sending them, and a collection of code used by both. The declaration did not make every piece of writing or every image on the Web free for anyone to use.

The release included not only programs in a form computers could run, but also their "source code," the instructions written in a form people could read. By examining source code, people could find out what the software was doing inside.

A technical document from 1992 shows that, in the line-mode browser, the part that handled user input and the part that displayed text on the screen were kept in separate files. What looked like one continuous action on the screen was divided into different tasks within the code. Having access to the code meant people could work out which part they might change.

Yet being able to read code was not the same as having permission to distribute a modified program. In its 1993 declaration, CERN gave everyone permission to use, copy, modify, and redistribute the software. Those who received it could examine how it worked, make changes of their own, and pass their versions on to others.

The following year, in 1994, CERN changed the way it released a new version of its server software.

Under the previous year's declaration, CERN had relinquished its intellectual property rights to the code. This time, CERN retained the copyright while granting others permission to use the software. That did not mean people now had to pay to use it. They were still allowed to copy, modify, and distribute it. But products containing CERN's code now had to acknowledge where that code came from.

Why did CERN keep the copyright?

On November 15, 1994, François Flückiger, who led CERN's Web development team, explained that he wanted to prevent third parties from turning freely available software into proprietary software and denying others the right to use it. According to his explanation, retaining the copyright was intended to help keep CERN's software freely available and make clear who had created it.

The terms of the 1994 license, however, required acknowledgment of CERN's code but did not require modified versions to be distributed under the same free terms as the original. Those who made modified versions could choose their own licensing terms. Being able to use software received from CERN freely was not the same as having a guarantee that every later version would offer the same freedoms.

In July 1995, the Massachusetts Institute of Technology (MIT) in the United States released version 3.1 of the server software, based on CERN's version 3.0. MIT used licensing terms of its own choosing and kept a notice acknowledging that the software included code created by CERN. Software developed at one research institution had become a new version in the hands of another.

Back at the opening screen, entering [1] takes you to the next document. The software that delivered such documents was passed on to new developers as well. The version released by MIT still carried CERN's name, identifying the source of part of its code.

Georgia, one of the southeastern states of the United States, has the vast blue expanse of the Atlantic Ocean to its right, if we use a map with north at the top as our reference. There, where the land meets the sea, a horizon stretches out, seemingly connecting reality with infinity.

The Atlantic is beautiful not only because of the vastness of its waters, but also because of the strength and serenity it conveys. Its waves create a constant rhythm, its reflections change with the sunlight, and its shores offer landscapes capable of inspiring admiration and tranquility. Looking out over it reminds us that beyond our cities, roads, and everyday concerns, there is an immense natural world that continues to move to its own rhythm.

And yet, there is even more beyond that eastern horizon. Beyond the Atlantic lies a vast world of other shores, distant lands, different cultures, and countless stories waiting to be discovered. The ocean does not mark the end of the world; it opens the way to another part of it. What appears to be the farthest edge of our view is, in reality, only the beginning of a much greater horizon.
From Georgia, the Atlantic Ocean represents an extraordinary natural presence—a place of beauty, life, and connection with the world. Its horizon invites us to look farther, appreciate what we have close to us, and understand that sometimes, all it takes is pausing by the sea to discover something truly beautiful—and to remember that there is always more beyond what we can see.

text:
Brad Pitt offered Angelina Jolie $54.5 million for her half of the château where they got married. She took $64 million from a Russian vodka billionaire instead.

In the video below, a year after the wedding, they sit side by side on TV and joke about what ten years of marriage will do to them. Less than a year later, she filed for divorce.

They bought Château Miraval in 2008 for $37.5 million. His company owned 60%, hers 40%.

A few months before the wedding, he gave her another 10%. Now they were equal partners.

He threw himself into the wine. By 2021 the business was bringing in more than $50 million a year.

Then came the divorce.

She had agreed to his $54.5 million. The deal died over one clause. She says he wanted her to sign something that would stop her from ever talking about his behaviour during the marriage. She refused.

So she sold to the Stoli vodka group, controlled by Russian-born billionaire Yuri Shefler. Pitt says he never got a say.

He says they had agreed neither would ever sell without the other's consent. His lawyers say she let a stranger into his home.

Her side hit back. They say he spent the winery's money on his own projects, a house, a pool, a recording studio, so that she would "never see a dime."

And one detail tells you how far it went.

Pitt went to a court in Luxembourg to take back the 10% he gave her before the wedding.

They said their vows in that chapel. Four years later, they're still fighting over who gets to keep the walls.

Did Jolie have every right to sell her half, or did she sell his home to hurt him?

text:
Part II

Benedicamus Domino! He does not leave us orphans!

The Holy Eucharist

22. The Holy Eucharist had for you many joys and advantages when you were able to participate in this Sacrament of Love, but now that you are deprived of it for being defenders of the truth and justice, your advantages are the same. For who would have dared approach this fearsome table if Jesus Christ had not given us a precept, and if the Church, which desires that we fortify ourselves with this Bread of Life, had not invited us to eat by the voice of its ministers, who re-clothed us with a nuptial dress. All was obedience, but if we compare obedience by that which we are deprived of, with that which led us there, it will be easy to judge the merit. Abraham obeyed in immolating his son, and in not immolating him, but his obedience was greater when he took the sword in his hand than when he returned it to its scabbard. We are obedient in going to Communion, but in holding ourselves from the sacrifice we are immolating Ourselves. Quenched of the thirst of justice and deprived of the Blood of the Lamb which alone can slake it, we sacrifice our own liking as much as it is in us to do. The sacrifice of Abraham was for an instant, and an angel stopped the knife, ours is daily, renewing itself everyday, every time that we adore with submission the Hand of God which drives us away from His altars, and this sacrifice is voluntary. It is to be advantageously deprived of the Eucharist, to raise the standard of the Cross for the cause of Christ and the Glory of His Church. Observe, my children, that Jesus, after having given His Body, found no difficulty in dying for us. There is the action of a Christian in the persecutions; the cross follows on from the Eucharist. Let not the love for the Eucharist drive us away from the cross. It is to arise and make glorious advance in the grace of the gospel, to go out from the Cenacle, to go to Calvary. Yes, I have no fear in saying it. When the storm of the malice of men roars against truth and justice, it is more advantageous to the faithful to suffer for Christ than to participate in His Body by Communion. I seem to hear the Savior saying to us, Do not be afraid to be separated from My table for the confession of My Name: it is a grace I give you, which is very rare. Repair by this humiliating deprivation which glorifies Me, all the Communions which dishonor me. Feel this grace. You can do nothing for me, and I put into your hands a means of doing what I have done for you, and to return to Me with magnificence, that which I have given you in the greatest measure. I have given you My Body, and you give it back to Me. since you are separated from It in My service. You give back the truth which you have received from My love. I could not have given you anything greater. Your gratitude matches that; the grace I have given you - the greatest of the Gifts I made to you. Console yourselves if I do not call upon you to pour out your blood like the martyrs; there is mine to make up for it. Every time that you are prevented from drinking It, I regard it the same as if you had spilt yours; and Mine is more precious.”

23. So that is how we find the Eucharist, even during the deprivation of the Eucharist. From another viewpoint, who is able to separate us from Christ and His Church in Communion in approaching its altars by faith in a much more efficacious manner since it is spiritual and further from the senses. It is what I call communicating spiritually in uniting oneself with the faithful who are able to do it in different places on earth. You were familiar with this sort of Communion in the times when you were able to go to the Holy Table. You knew the advantages and the manner of it, so I shall not discuss it with you, but I am going to show you what Holy Scripture and the annals of the Church offer in reflections on the deprivation of the Mass, and the necessity of continual sacrifice for the faithful in times of persecution.

24. Give particular attention, my children, to the principles I am giving to recall. They are for your edification. Nothing happens without the Will of God! Whether we have a worship which allows us to assist at Mass, or that we be deprived of it, let us submit to His Holy Will, but in all circumstances let us be worthy. The worship which we owe to Christ depends on the assistance which He gives us and the necessity we have of His help. This worship outlines for us our duties as isolated faithful just as it was outlined for us before, in the public exercise of our religion. As children of God, according to the witness of Sts. Peter and John, we participated in the Priesthood of Jesus Christ to offer prayers and promises. If we are not entitled to sacrifice on visible altars, we are not without offering, since we can offer it in worship by our love in sacrificing Christ ourselves to His Father on the invisible altar of our hearts. Faithful to this principle, we shall gather all the graces that we would have been able to gather had we been able to assist at the Holy Sacrifice of the Mass. Charity unites us to all the faithful of the universe who offer this Divine Sacrifice, or who assist at it. If we lack a material altar and sensible species, there are no longer any in heaven where Jesus Christ is offered in the most perfect manner. Yes, my children, the faithful who are without priest, offer their sacrifices without temple, without minister and without anything sensible. It needs only Jesus Christ to offer it. ‘For the sacrifice of the heart, where the Victim must be consumed by the fire of love for the Holy Ghost, it requires to be united to Jesus Christ,” said St. Clement of Alexandria, ‘by words, by deeds and by heart. We are united to Him by words when they are true, by our actions when they are just, by our hearts when charity inflames them. So, let us speak the truth, follow nothing but the truth, love nothing but the truth. Then we shall render to God the glory which is His due. When we are true in our words, just in our actions, submit to God in our desires and thoughts, in speaking for Him alone, in praising Him for His gifts, in humiliating ourselves for our sins, we offer God an agreeable sacrifice, and which cannot be taken from us. It remains for me to consider the Eucharist as a last sacrament. You could be deprived of It at death, so I must enlighten you and caution you against so terrible a deprivation.

Last Sacrament

25. God, Who loves and protects us, wishes to give us His Body at the approach of death -- to take away our fear on this last journey. When you look to the future and see yourself on your own deathbed, without the Last Sacrament, without Extreme Unction and without any help on the part of the ministers of the Lord, you see yourself abandoned in the most sad and terrible way. Console yourselves, my children, in the trust you have in God. This tender Father will pour on you His graces, His blessings and His mercies, in these awful moments which you fear, in more abundance than if you were being assisted by His ministers of whom you have been deprived only because you would not abandon Him Himself. The abandonment and forsakenness which we fear for ourselves, resembles that of the Savior on the Cross when He said to His Father: My God, My God, why have You forsaken me? (Psalm 21) Ah! How constructive and consoling are these words! Your pains and abandonment lead you to your Glorious Destiny in Ending Your Life like Jesus ended His. Jesus, in His sufferings, His abandonment and His death, was in most intimate union with His Father. In your pains and abandonment, be to Him likewise united, and let your last sign be like His, that God’s will be done. Being deprived of Extreme Unction, and in the hands of persons, who not only do not help, but also insult me, I shall be much happier that my death shall have more conformity with that of Jesus Who was a spectacle of opprobrium to all the world. Crucified by the hands of His enemies, He was treated like a thief and died between two thieves. He was wisdom Itself and was taken for an idiot. He was truth, and He was taken for a cheat and deceiver. The Pharisees and scribes triumphed over Him and in His presence. They were finally sated with His Blood. Christ died in the torture and excruciating pains of the Cross. Christians, if your last moment and death are an occasion for your enemies to treat you with insults and disgrace, what were those of Jesus? I am not sure that the angel who was sent to make up for the hard heartedness and callousness of men was not to teach us, that in similar circumstances, we receive the consolation of Heaven when that of men is missing. It was not without a special plan of God, that the Apostles who ought to have consoled Jesus, remained in a deep sleep. So the faithful should not be surprised to find himself without a priest in his last moments. Jesus reproached His apostles that they slept, but He did not say that they left Him without consolation, to teach us, that if we go into the Garden of Olives, if we climb up to Calvary, if we die alone and without human help, God watches over us, consoles us, and that suffices. Faithful, you are afraid of what follows the present time. Lift your eyes up to Jesus; keep them on Him; contemplate Him. He is your Model.

26. After having contemplated on Him, could you still fear the deprivation of prayers and ceremonies of the Church which was established to sanctify and honor our last moments, our death and burial? Remember that the cause for which we suffer and die gives to this deprivation a new glory and gives to us the merit of the last bit of resemblance we can have to Jesus Christ. Providence has wished and permitted for our instruction, that the Pharisees should put guards at the Sepulchre to guard the Body of Jesus Crucified. It has even wished that after His death His Body should remain in the hands of His enemies, and that in order to teach us that however long the domination of our enemies be, we must suffer it with patience and pray for them. St. Ignatius, the Martyr, who had so much ardor to be eaten by wild beasts, did not he prefer to have them for a sepulchre than the most beautiful mausoleum? Even the first Christians who were delivered to the executioner, all the confessors and all the martyrs, never worried about their last moment nor their graves. None of them worried on what should become of their bodies. Yes, my children, when one has trusted Jesus Christ all his life, he still trusts Him after his death. Jesus on the Cross and near to death, saw the women who had followed Him from Galilee. His Mother and Mary Magdalene and His beloved Apostle were near the Cross in sorrow, silence and grief. There, my children, is the picture you shall see, Most Christians feel sorry for those among the faithful who find themselves persecuted, but they keep themselves apart, while some like the Mother of Jesus go to the innocent, which wickedness strikes down. I remark with St. Ambrose, that Jesus’ Mother, who stayed at the foot of the Cross, knew that her Son was dying for the redemption of mankind, and wishing to die with Him for the accomplishment of this great work, she did not tear to annoy the Jews with her presence and desired to die with her Son. When you see someone die all forsaken, my children, or by the sword of persecution, imitate the Mother of Jesus, and not the women who had followed Him from Galilee, but kept back at the foot of the Cross. Be pierced with this truth: that the most glorious and salutary time to die is when virtue is strongest in our heart. One must never fear for a friend of Jesus Christ when he is suffering. Help him even by our looks and our tears. That, my children is what I believe I had to tell you. I believe it sufficient to answer your questions and calm your fears. I have put the principles without going into detail, which appears useless. Your reflections will certainly make up for it, and our conversations if providence ever permits, shall be on what you have done and what will inspire you to new desires.

27. I must tell you, my children, not to worry at what you are witnessing. Faith is not allied to these terrors. The number of the elect was always small. Only fear that God does not reproach you for lack of faith, and for not having been able to watch an hour with Him. I admit, however, that humanity can grieve, but in so saying, I shall add that faith must gladden. God does all. Bear this judgment. It is the only one worthy of you. The unbelievers themselves delivered this judgment when the Savior was making miraculous cures. What He is doing now is far greater. In His mortal life He cured the body, but now He cures souls and completes by trials the number of the elect.

28. Whatever are God’s plans for us, let us adore the depth of His judgments and put all our confidence in Him. If He wishes to deliver us, the time is near. Everything turns against us, our friends oppress us; our relations treat us like strangers; the faithful who used to worship with us are turned away with a single look. We do not fear to say that they are not only unlike us, they are faithful to their country and submit to its laws (right or wrong) and also claim to be faithful to God. They fear to say that they love us, or even know us. If we are without help along side men, we are assured of Gods help, who according to the Prophet King, will deliver the poor from the powerful, for they have no other help.

29. The universe is the work of God. He reigns over it, and every happening is according to the plans of His providence. When we believe that desertion is going to be general, we forget that a little faith is enough to give faith to the family of Jesus - like a little leaven makes all the dough rise. These extraordinary events where the mob wields the ax to undermine the work of God, serve marvelously to show His omnipotence. In every country will be seen what the people of God saw. When the Lord was wanted by Gideon to show His power against the Midianites, He had him send back most of his army. Three hundred men only and those without arms in order that it could be seem that the victory was God’s. This small number of Gideon’s soldiers, is the number of the faithful elect of this century. You have seen with the saddest astonishment, my children, that out of all those called, since all of France was Christian, the greater part, like Gideon’s army, remained weak, timid and fearing to lose their temporal interests. God sends them back, for use in His justice. God only wants those who give themselves to Him entirely. Do not be surprised at the great number who quit. Truth wins, no matter how small the number of those who love and remain attached to Him. For my part I nave only one wish, the desire of St. Paul. As a child of the Church, as a soldier of Christ I wish to die under His standard.

30. If you have the works of St. Cyprian, read them, my children. One must go back to the first centuries of the Church to find worthy examples to serve as models. It is in these holy books and in those of the first defenders of the faith that one must form a precise idea of the object of martyrdom and of the confession of Jesus Christ. It is truth and justice. These are the august, eternal and unchangeable objects of the faith which one must confess. It is the gospel. For human instructions, however wise they may be, they are temporary and changeable. But the gospel and the law of God holds for eternity. It is in thinking over this distinction that you will clearly see what is God’s and what is Caesars. As by the example of Christ you must render to One with respect, and to the other that which is his due.

31. Every century, the Church is in agreement, that there is nothing more glorious and holy than to confess the Name of Jesus Christ. But remember, my dear children, to confess it in a manner worthy of the crown which we desire. It is during the time one suffers most that one must have the greatest holiness. I can find nothing more beautiful than the words of St. Cyprian when he praises all the Christian virtues in the confessors of Jesus Christ. “You have always observed,” he says to them, “the command of the Lord with a severity worthy of your firmness, you have conserved simplicity and innocence, charity and concord, modesty and humility. You have carried out your ministry with care and exactitude. You have been vigilant to help those who need help, to have compassion for the poor, of constancy in defending the truth and discipline, in order that there be nothing wanting in these great examples of virtue which you have till now given. It is by your confession and generous sufferings that you highly animate your brethren to martyrdom and to show then the road.”

32. I hope, children, although God does not call you to martyrdom nor to a distressing confession of His Name, to be able to speak to you one day as in the example of this illustrious martyr when he spoke to the confessors Celerius and Areie, and to praise in you your humility rather than your steadfastness and to glorify you more for your holiness than for your sufferings and wounds. In looking towards this happy moment, profit from my advice and sustain yourselves by my example, if necessary.

33. God watches over us; our hope is justified. It shows us either that the persecution stops, or the persecution will be our crown. In the alternative of one or the other, I see the accomplishment of our destiny. Let God’s will be done, since in whatever manner He delivers us, His eternal mercies pour into us. I end, my dear children, in embracing you and praying to God for your as my faith and as my sincere resignation is to have no other will than that of God.

IV. Saul Had a Crown, an Army, and a Sword—but Lost the Kingdom Through Disobedience

1 Samuel 13:8–14, 19–22; 15:17–23; 17:47

First Samuel 13 brings us to one of the decisive failures in Saul’s reign. The Philistines have assembled against Israel, the people are distressed, and Saul’s forces are under tremendous pressure. Samuel has instructed Saul concerning the appointed time, but the prophet has not yet appeared when Saul decides to proceed with the offering. Afterward, Saul explains his reasoning. The people were scattering, the Philistines were gathering, and he feared that the enemy would descend upon him before he had made supplication unto the LORD. Then comes the revealing statement in 1 Samuel 13:12: “I forced myself therefore, and offered a burnt offering.” That is an interesting confession. Saul presents his disobedience as though circumstances compelled him to do something he really did not want to do. He was under pressure, the situation looked unfavorable, and the religious act appeared necessary. But Samuel does not congratulate him for finding an emergency solution. He answers, “Thou hast done foolishly: thou hast not kept the commandment of the LORD thy God” (verse 13). The offense was not that Saul lacked military courage or failed to devise an impressive strategy. He had disobeyed God’s command. Think about the irony. Israel had requested a king who would fight its battles, but the king’s decisive failure was his unwillingness to submit to the authority of the God who could win those battles. He did not need more impressive qualifications. He needed obedience. And there is a tremendous lesson in that for anyone entrusted with responsibility. Pressure does not automatically turn disobedience into wisdom. An emergency does not grant a man authority God never gave him. A religious action does not become acceptable simply because it was performed for what the man considered a worthwhile purpose. Saul had a problem, and he attempted to solve it by crossing the boundary of the instruction given to him. He may have looked religious while doing it, but Samuel identified the matter for what it was. He had not kept the commandment of the LORD.

Now notice the material conditions of Israel’s military forces in the same chapter. First Samuel 13:19 explains that there was no smith found throughout the land of Israel because the Philistines had prevented the Hebrews from making swords or spears. Verse 22 consequently records, “So it came to pass in the day of battle, that there was neither sword nor spear found in the hand of any of the people that were with Saul and Jonathan: but with Saul and with Jonathan his son was there found.” That is a remarkable military disadvantage. Israel possessed a king but lacked the ability to equip most of its soldiers with the principal weapons available to its enemies. Saul and Jonathan had swords, but the majority of the force did not. The nation had obtained the political institution it demanded, yet the institution could not simply manufacture military superiority by existing. A crown does not produce a sword. A royal title does not create an armoury. And even a complete armoury cannot compel God to bless disobedience. The situation also prepares us for Jonathan’s extraordinary statement in the following chapter, because Jonathan will declare that the LORD can save by many or by few while Israel is suffering from a serious shortage of equipment. The lesson is not that weapons are sinful. The Bible records the legitimate use of weapons by faithful men, and David himself will later employ Goliath’s sword. The issue is the insufficiency of material strength as a replacement for the LORD’s power. Men can become so fascinated with the instruments of warfare that they forget the authority under which those instruments are supposed to operate. Israel had requested a human champion, but human champions still needed weapons, soldiers, supplies, discipline,

.
This holy Archangel identified himself to the exiled Jew Tobias as one of the Seven who stand before God(Tob. 12:15). His name means the healing of God, and he is thought to be the Angel who came down and agitated the water of the pool of Bethsaida in Jerusalem. The sick, who always lay around the pool, strove to be the first to enter the water afterwards, because that fortunate one was always cured. We read of this in the story of the paralytic cured by Jesus, who had waited patiently for thirty-eight years, unable to move when the occasion presented itself. (Cf. John 5:1-9)
.
Saint Raphael is best known through the beautiful history of the two Tobias, father and son, exiled to Persia in the days of the Assyrian conquest in the eighth century before Christ. In their story, the Archangel plays the major role.
.
The father Tobias was a faithful son of Jacob and was old and worn out by his manifold good works; for many years he had assisted his fellow exiles in every possible way, even burying the slain of Israel during a persecution by Sennacherib, and continuing this practice despite the wrath that king manifested towards him. Having been stripped of all his possessions, he desired to have his son recover a substantial sum of money he had once lent to a member of his family in a distant city. He needed a companion for the young Tobias. God provided that guide in the Archangel Raphael, whom the son met providentially one day, in the person of a stranger from the very area where he was to go, in the country of the Medes. Raphael to all appearances was a young man like himself, who said his name was Azarias (Assistance of God).Everything went well, as proposed; the young Tobias recovered the sum and then was married, during their stay in Media, to the virtuous daughter of another relative, whom Providence had reserved for him.
.
All aspects of this journey had been thorny with difficulties, but the wise guide had found a way to overcome all of them. When a huge fish threatened to devour Tobias, camped on the shores of the Tigris, the guide told him how to remove it from the water, and the fish expired at his feet; then remedies and provisions were derived from this creature by the directives of Azarias. When the Angel led Tobias for lodging in the city of Rages, to the house of his kinsman Raguel, father of the beautiful Sara, the young man learned that seven proposed husbands had died on the very day of the planned marriage. How would Tobias fare? The Angel reassured him that this would not be his own fate, and told him to pray with his future spouse for three nights, that they might be blessed with a holy posterity. Sara was an only daughter, as Tobias was an only son, and she was endowed with a large heritage.
.
During the absence of the young Tobias, his father had become blind when the droppings of a pigeon had fallen into his eyes. When the two travelers returned after an extended absence, which had cost his mother many tears, the young Tobias was deeply grieved to find his father unable to see him and his new daughter-in-law. But Raphael told the son how to cure his father's blindness by means of the gall of the fish; and after the remedy had proved efficacious, all of them rejoiced time in their blessings.
.
When Tobias the son narrated his story and told his father that all their benefits had come to them through this stranger, both father and son wished to give Azarias half of the inheritance. Raphael declined and revealed his identity, saying he was sent to assist the family of the man who had never failed to obey and honor the blessed God of Israel. Raphael, before he disappeared, said to the family: It is honorable to reveal and confess the works of God. Prayer is good, with fasting and alms, more than to lay up treasures, for alms deliver from death and purge away sins, and cause the giver to find mercy and life everlasting... When thou didst pray with tears and didst bury the dead, and didst leave thy dinner to hide the dead by day in thy house, and bury them by night, I offered thy prayer to the Lord. And because thou wast acceptable to God, it was necessary that trials prove thee... I am the Angel Raphael, one of the seven who stand before the Lord.
.
Eternal Father, I wish to honor St. Raphael the Archangel, and I give Thee thanks for all the graces Thou hast bestowed upon him. I ask Thee to please increase grace in my soul through the merits of this saint, and I commit the end of my life to him by this special prayer, so that by virtue of Thy goodness and promise, St. Raphael the Archangel might be my advocate and provide whatever is needed at that hour. Amen.
